elements.element: Audit no more than once per 12 months
elements.evidence: not more than once in any twelve (12) month period
on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
to review or audit during normal business hours

elements.element: Audit performed by an independent auditor
elements.evidence: clause retains 'Any Party shall have the right ... to review or audit'; no independent auditor requirement inserted
no confidentiality undertaking appears anywhere in 9.8 or 9.9
shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying with the review or audit

elements.element: Cost shifts to Customer only where underpayment exceeds 5%
elements.evidence: no underpayment threshold; cost allocation left as 'the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying'

elements.element: No direct access to Customer systems
elements.evidence: scope remains 'the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs' with no express bar on system access
not more than once in any twelve (12) month period
not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice

elements.element: Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10%
elements.evidence: audited Party 'shall be permitted to recover ... the entire costs' with no underpayment carve-out or 10% threshold

offending_extra_words: Any Party shall have the right, not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice, to review or audit during normal business hours the relevant books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs pursuant to this Paragraph 9.
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the edit only adds frequency, notice and business-hours limits. The independent-auditor requirement, the auditor confidentiality undertaking, and the express bar on direct access to Customer systems are absent, so the preferred level is incomplete.

Cost allocation: the retained sentence puts compliance costs on the requesting Party, which is favourable, but neither the 5% (preferred) nor 10% (fallback) underpayment shifting threshold is present, so that element is not expressly met at either level.
Fallback also fails on the cost/underpayment threshold element, so no level is complete on its own terms.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrote the whole opening sentence (24 to 49 words, ratio 2.04) when a short inserted qualifier ('not more than once in any twelve (12) month period, on thirty (30) days' prior written notice and during normal business hours') would suffice; the official minimality gate returned not ok.
Intent is preserved: the F&ASC exclusivity in 9.9, the Schedule B proportional recovery and the existing cost allocation remain effective and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.
Margin comment offers 15 days' notice, but promises in the comment are non-operative and cannot cure the missing operative elements.
